summary: Research-only recommendation for reliable API-first chat and structured model outputs

findings.conclusion: Free-form chat is a POST /api/sessions/{session_id}/turns SSE stream with meta, delta, citation, done, and error events. Structured generation is centralized in app/llm/structured.py and app/llm/notes.py: complete_json requests ordinary model text, parse_json extracts an apparent first JSON object or array including fenced output, manual validation follows, one corrective retry is attempted, and plan/question fragment salvage may return partial data. app/models.py has Plan, PlanNode, QuizQuestionInput, and Message, but output models currently allow coercion and ignore unknown fields by default. Mermaid is rendered in the browser from a CDN and has no server-side syntax-validation contract.

findings.topic: Pydantic discriminated unions and strict boundaries
findings.conclusion: Pydantic recommends discriminated unions because a discriminator selects exactly one member, is more predictable and efficient than untagged unions, and produces an OpenAPI discriminator. Pydantic validates untrusted data and emits JSON Schema; ordinary validation may coerce values and extra fields are ignored by default. Configure output models with ConfigDict(extra='forbid') and strict scalar types where coercion could conceal malformed model output. Use TypeAdapter for reusable union validation and model_json_schema() as the API/provider schema source.

FastAPI response_model or a typed return annotation validates returned data, emits JSON Schema/OpenAPI, serializes through Pydantic, and filters undeclared fields. This is appropriate for a structured artifact endpoint. Existing SSE should remain a direct StreamingResponse path because it is a stream rather than a completed JSON response.

OpenAI Structured Outputs uses strict JSON Schema and is preferable to JSON mode when supported: JSON mode guarantees valid JSON but not schema adherence, while strict Structured Outputs targets the supplied schema. Provider documentation also calls out refusal and incomplete or max-token cases. Sage uses an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint, so response_format/json_schema support must be capability-detected or configured rather than assumed; local Pydantic validation remains mandatory even when provider enforcement is enabled.

The official Mermaid API exposes mermaid.parse(text, parseOptions) specifically for syntax validation without rendering. It returns a diagram type on success and throws or returns false with suppressErrors on failure. Client code should parse before rendering and use strict security for model-generated untrusted text. The parser is JavaScript, not a Python FastAPI library, so validation should be isolated behind an adapter rather than reimplementing Mermaid grammar in Python.

A pinned Node worker or sidecar importing Mermaid and calling parse is the highest-fidelity option and avoids Chromium. @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/mmdc can validate by rendering to SVG but adds Chromium/process overhead and a larger operations surface; its README says its Node API is not covered by semver. PyPI mermaid-parser-py 0.0.4 wraps the original JS parser through PythonMonkey, requires Node.js, and documents deprecated mermaidAPI plus browser hot patches, so it is a third-party prototype rather than an official stable parser. A regex or pure-Python subset is fast but cannot claim compatibility with the browser renderer.

Mermaid documents strict security behavior, and its API source contains a 50,000-character maximum diagram text length. Sage should impose a smaller application limit, strip only one outer Markdown fence, reject HTML/script/directive features unless explicitly required, validate before persistence, and render with strict security. Client parse/render errors are useful UX feedback but cannot replace server validation when the API promises reliable artifacts.

Sage already makes one bounded corrective retry for plans, generic questions, notes questions, and answerability checks. _plan_from_fragments can invent step keys and discard dependencies; _questions_from_fragments keeps individually valid questions. This is useful for independent quiz items but unsafe as a general correctness promise for dependency-aware plans or Mermaid. First-bracket extraction can also accept malformed JSON with trailing prose. Every recovery result must pass the same final decoder, Pydantic schema, and semantic validators.

recommendations: Keep POST /api/sessions/{id}/turns as free-form SSE. Stream deltas for low latency, persist final text and citations, and mark EOF-before-done or provider interruption as partial rather than successful.

Add one API-first structured artifact operation, for example POST /api/sessions/{id}/outputs, whose request selects output_kind: chat, mermaid, todo, or quiz. Prefer separate provider schemas per kind over one large union, then return a stable envelope containing schema_version, output_id, session_id, kind, content, citations, and validation metadata. The response union should be discriminated by kind using Literal values and Field(discriminator='kind').

Make envelope fields server-owned. The model should produce content only; the server assigns output_id, schema_version, item IDs, positions, timestamps, citations, and validation status. Do not use model-generated IDs as persistence keys.

Use conservative content models: chat.content is bounded and non-empty; mermaid has title plus plain source code with no Markdown fence and a server-derived diagram_type; todo has a bounded title and 1-100 ordered items with bounded text and strict boolean done; quiz reuses 2-6 options and correct_index rules while enforcing strict difficulty 1-5 and unique non-empty options. Set ConfigDict(extra='forbid'), use strict scalar types where applicable, and normalize only deterministic presentation details such as one outer fence removal, trimming, and line-ending normalization.

Implement one shared staged decoder: reject empty output; remove BOM and at most one complete json fence; parse exactly one JSON value with no trailing non-whitespace; validate with TypeAdapter or model_validate; run semantic validators for duplicates, bounds, dependency references and cycles, correct_index, and Mermaid syntax; serialize only the validated model. Do not use permissive first-bracket extraction as final acceptance.

For Mermaid, use a validator adapter with a pinned Node runtime or sidecar calling official mermaid.parse(text, {suppressErrors: false}) and returning diagram_type plus a sanitized error. Prefer this over mmdc because parse avoids Chromium/rendering overhead. Treat mermaid-parser-py as optional prototype only. If Node cannot be deployed, feature-flag Mermaid as unverified or reject structured Mermaid requests; do not claim server reliability from client-only parsing.

Use provider strict JSON Schema when the configured OpenAI-compatible model advertises response_format/json_schema support; otherwise use the same schema in the prompt and local validation. Capability failure should fall back to ordinary JSON prompting rather than fail every chat request. Cache schemas per output kind and keep provider schema features within its supported subset.

Recover malformed model output with at most one repair attempt. Send original model text plus bounded field-level validation errors and exact schema requirements; never trust the repair until decode, Pydantic, and semantic validation pass. Handle refusal, incomplete/max-token output, empty content, and transport errors distinctly. After repair fails, return a retryable 422 model_output envelope without raw model output; log only a redacted hash, kind, attempt count, and validation codes.

Allow conservative partial salvage only for independent quiz items when every retained item validates and the requested minimum count is met. Do not salvage Mermaid, free-form chat, or dependency-aware todos/plans by inventing missing structure. Existing plan fragment salvage should be removed or explicitly marked degraded because synthesizing keys while discarding dependencies changes semantics.

Use Sage's existing typed error envelope for structured failures with code model_output, retryable true for bounded malformed-output recovery, and stable detail fields such as kind, attempt, and issue codes. Add contract tests for fenced or trailing JSON, wrong discriminator, extra fields, coercion, duplicate IDs, invalid quiz indexes, dependency cycles, Mermaid parse failures, provider refusal/incomplete responses, repair success, and repair exhaustion.
